newsitem.title: FRANCE: Charter airlines boosted by French truck strike.
newsitem.headline: Charter airlines boosted by French truck strike.

text.p: French cargo charter airlines are being inundated with inquiries on ad hoc flights from shippers and forwarders whose traffic is being disrupted because of road blocks set up all over the country by striking lorry drivers, airline sources said.

"The telephone hasn't stop ringing for the past week and we have been operating two to three flights per day on behalf of customers who normally use road transport for shipments," an official for Marseille-based Air Provence International, told Reuters.
The most popular routes had been Paris-Marseille, Paris-Toulouse and Marseille-Lyon using Air Provence's fleet of three-tonne capacity Grumann G159s and 5.6-tonne capacity HS748, the official added.
"We've had to turn down requests to operate cargo charter services to Madrid and Stuttgart because our fleet and crews were fully deployed," he added.
Another cargo charter airline, Transvalair, said it too had received a lot of calls from forwarding agents in the past 24 hours who were considering transferring freight from road to air.
"In most cases, they simply wanted information on what we could offer in the event of the lorry drivers' action being prolonged," a Transvalair official said.

This evening, Transvalair had charted a 30-tonne capacity Short Belfast aircraft from Heavylift Airlines to operate between Paris and Stansted carrying a truck load of freight which had been trapped in road blocks near the French capital, the official added. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
